summary: Feed s066_single is degraded: 58.0% of TCP sessions (69/119) are one-way, violating APM requirement for bidirectional visibility. All other checks (duplicates, encryption, VLANs, drops, overload) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker / TAP/SPAN is forwarding only one direction to the APM. 69 of 119 TCP sessions show only one direction (58.0% vs 10% threshold), indicating asymmetric routing with single-sided SPAN or broker not aggregating both sides of the flow to the same tool port.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM needs_both_directions=true to correlate request/response and measure latency/transaction time. With 58% one-way flows it sees incomplete transactions, cannot calculate response times accurately, and will miss performance anomalies and generate false incomplete-flow alerts.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each session to the same APM tool port so the APM receives complete client-server exchanges for accurate timing and transaction reconstruction.
